title: DADI 2H (NSIC Rc 788H) Hybrid Rice: Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaTitle: DADI 2H (NSIC Rc 788H): Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaDescription: DADI 2H is NSIC Rc 788H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland approved in 2026. See its pest ratings, grain quality and where it grows best.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 788H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as DADI 2H and known locally as Mestiso 158. The NSIC approved it in 2026. Philippine Dadi Agricultural Technology bred it. Its days to harvest and trial yield are not published yet, but its pest ratings and grain quality are below.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for DADI 2H, or rice variety 788H, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Watch out for:** brown planthopper, stem borer, tungro.
**Cooked rice:** low amylose, so soft and tender.

blocks.text: How many days does it take, and how much does it yield?

This variety's days to harvest and trial yields are not published yet. So ask the seed seller or your municipal agriculturist for the figures from the trials in your region before you plan the season. Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it. Meanwhile, our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare) covers the habits that matter with any variety.

blocks.text: So scout early for [brown planthopper](/pests/brown-planthopper), [stem borer](/pests/rice-stem-borer), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.
Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is DADI 2H the same as NSIC Rc 788H?
items.a: Yes. DADI 2H is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 788H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 158. The numbers on this page are for NSIC Rc 788H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 788H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 158. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.
The NSIC approved it in 2026. Philippine Dadi Agricultural Technology bred it. Its days to harvest and trial yield are not published yet, so ask for the regional trial figures before you plant.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against brown planthopper, stem borer, tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has low amylose, 12.4 percent. So it cooks soft.
